sentences.text: By means of this third bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant Anuj Kumar, who is involved in Case Crime No. 351 of 2020, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, police station Kishni, district Mainpuri, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: The first and second bail applications of the applicant were rejected vide orders dated 28.07.2021 and 09.01.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application Nos. 6049 of 2021 and 17431 of 2022 on merits.

sentences.text: Main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant has been languishing in jail since 24.08.2020 but till date, his trial has not been concluded on account of slackness on the part of the prosecution, therefore, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned A.G.A. for the State vehemently opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that in this case, victim is minor and she has already been examined before the trial Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: The second bail application of the applicant was rejected considering the statement of the victim given before the trial Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: So far as delay in concluding the trial of the applicant is concerned, it is argued that, out of 10 prosecution witnesses, 03 prosecution witnesses including the victim have been examined before the trial Court and on 12 dates, case was adjourned on account of delaying tactics adopted by co-accused.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is also submitted that efforts shall be made to produce remaining prosecution witnesses for early conclusion of the trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Hence, bail application of the applicant is liable to be rejected.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Having heard the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perusing the order-sheet, I find that vide order dated 07.08.2023, status report of the trial was called for from the concerned Presiding Officer, who in turn, submitted report dated 22.08.2023, which is on record, wherein it is mentioned that statement of the victim was completed on 14.07.2022.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: In the meantime, statement of the informant/PW-2 was also recorded on 27.04.2022.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: On 17.05.2022, statement of the Investigating Officer Jaikab Fernandez was recorded as PW-3 but no cross-examination was done by the accused Surjan.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Thereafter, notice under Section 350 Cr.P.C. was sent to witnessJaikab Fernandez but he did not appear.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is also mentioned that on account of death of Presiding Officer in a road accident, Court was vacant upto 29.04.2023.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Lastly, it is mentioned that all efforts are being made to get the trial of the accused concluded.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Under the circumstances of the case as noted above, this Court feels that it would be appropriate to issue direction to concerned Court below to conclude the trial within time-bound period.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Hence, prayer for bail of the applicant is refused.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: The bail application is rejected.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is made clear that the observation contained in the instant order is confined to the issue of bail and shall not affect the merit of the trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: However, the trial Court is directed to make an endeavour to conclude the trial of the applicant expeditiously preferably within a period of nine months from the date of production of a copy of this order without granting any unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Superintendent of Police, Mainpuri is directed to ensure production of remaining prosecution witnesses before the trial Court on the date fixed.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Registrar (Compliance) and learned Government Advocate of this Court shall communicate this order to the Superintendent of Police, Mainpuri for information and compliance.
sentences._hearing_file: Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: 8. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

sentences.text: 9. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

sentences.text: Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State.
opennyai_summary.16_January_2024__facts:
By means of this third bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant Anuj Kumar, who is involved in Case Crime No. 351 of 2020, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, police station Kishni, district Mainpuri, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.
The first and second bail applications of the applicant were rejected vide orders dated 28.07.2021 and 09.01.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application Nos. 6049 of 2021 and 17431 of 2022 on merits.
opennyai_summary.16_January_2024__arguments:
Main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant has been languishing in jail since 24.08.2020 but till date, his trial has not been concluded on account of slackness on the part of the prosecution, therefore, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
The second bail application of the applicant was rejected considering the statement of the victim given before the trial Court.
opennyai_summary.16_January_2024__decision:
Under the circumstances of the case as noted above, this Court feels that it would be appropriate to issue direction to concerned Court below to conclude the trial within time-bound period.
Hence, prayer for bail of the applicant is refused.
The bail application is rejected.
It is made clear that the observation contained in the instant order is confined to the issue of bail and shall not affect the merit of the trial.
However, the trial Court is directed to make an endeavour to conclude the trial of the applicant expeditiously preferably within a period of nine months from the date of production of a copy of this order without granting any unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties.
Superintendent of Police, Mainpuri is directed to ensure production of remaining prosecution witnesses before the trial Court on the date fixed.
Registrar (Compliance) and learned Government Advocate of this Court shall communicate this order to the Superintendent of Police, Mainpuri for information and compliance.

opennyai_summary.13_September_2024__ANALYSIS:
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with trial.
7. The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history.
8. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.
9. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.
The said principle has been reiterated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
10.
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
11.
Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
12. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.
No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.
opennyai_summary.13_September_2024__decision:
The bail application is allowed.
14. Let the applicant- Anuj Kumar, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
15. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
16. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
